html:
On 1 January 1986 Aruba left the Netherlands Antilles and became a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The status is called Status Aparte.

Arubans had long resented rule from Willemstad in Curacao. The leader Betico Croes campaigned for separation, and Arubans voted for it in 1977.

Aruba was meant to become fully independent in 1996, but its people chose to keep the tie. The closure of the Lago refinery in 1985 forced it to turn to tourism, now its main business. Its move led the way for the end of the Netherlands Antilles in 2010.
sum: On 1 January 1986 Aruba left the Netherlands Antilles and became a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The status is called Status Aparte.
